title: clawd-video — watercolor cartoon shorts as a Claude skill
creator: aadil6971
summary: A Claude Code plugin/skill that turns a short brief into a 8-20 s hand-painted watercolor cartoon MP4 with an original synthesized soundtrack. Claude writes one story.js (painted set, part-based character rig, pose-as-function-of-time timeline) and one score.mjs; a small engine handles one-time p5.brush painting, per-frame Canvas2D compositing, paper finish, headless-Chrome frame capture, FFmpeg encoding and loudness-normalized audio muxing. The skill is built around a render-look-fix loop with machine checks (motion pop detector, contact sheets, ffprobe, EBU R128).
what_is_shown: Two demo MP4s at 1920x1080/24fps with AAC audio: 'Clawd at the Desk' (15 s) — pixel-sprite Clawd peeks from behind a laptop, types with accelerating rhythm and flying code glyphs, catches a bug under a flipped mug with camera kick, screen turns green with glow rays and confetti, dance, bow; 'Bun and the Flower' (8 s) — ink-outlined storybook bunny hides behind a stump, hops with squash/stretch, picks a flower, spin-jumps with a petal burst, waves.

techniques.name: Pure function of time
techniques.how: Every frame is drawn from t alone with seeded RNG and no inter-frame state; renderer steps exactly i/FPS.
techniques.quality_lever: Deterministic, any-frame-addressable output enables stills QA, exact frame counts and automated pop detection.

techniques.name: Paint once, composite per frame
techniques.how: Static set, props and pigment swatches are painted a single time with p5.brush on a hidden WEBGL canvas and cached as 2D canvases; moving things are drawn per frame on top.
techniques.quality_lever: Rich organic watercolor texture without per-frame flicker or render cost.

techniques.name: Clip-to-outline sprites
techniques.how: Because brush pigment mixes with what is beneath, sprites are painted on paper and clipped to a path ~3 px outside the ink line when drawn; flipped views painted separately.
techniques.quality_lever: Avoids paper halos and wrong-reading mirrored props.

techniques.name: Occlusion by redrawing background
techniques.how: To hide a character behind an object, draw the character then redraw the cached background clipped to the object's outline; switch depth only when fully clear (e.g., top of a hop).
techniques.quality_lever: Cheap, convincing depth staging with no layering bugs.

techniques.name: Part-based rig with feet-origin
techniques.how: Characters are ordered parts (ellipse/rect/rrect/poly) with pivots, origin at the feet, body pose (x,y,sx,sy,rot,turn) plus per-part rot/offset/scale and an eye object with modes.
techniques.quality_lever: On-model consistency every frame; squash/stretch keeps feet planted; spins via turn=cos(angle) with back-view face hiding.

techniques.name: Animation principles with numbers
techniques.how: Reference table gives concrete 24 fps values: anticipation 0.15-0.3 s with sy 0.78-0.85, take-off stretch 1.25-1.3, landing squash via damped spring, volume preservation sx=1/sqrt(sy), blink 0.12-0.14 s, eyes 1.45x for surprise.
techniques.quality_lever: Turns vague 'make it bouncy' into parameterized, repeatable motion an LLM can apply reliably.

techniques.name: Speed limits and ghost smears
techniques.how: Motion over ~60 px/frame or ~0.7 rad/frame, or cycles above ~5 Hz, are treated as strobing; fix by spreading frames or drawing 1-2 translucent past-pose ghosts.
techniques.quality_lever: Smooth perceived motion at a low frame rate.

techniques.name: Beat-boundary pose blending
techniques.how: One branch per beat in poseAt(t); boundaries either start from the previous end values or blend over ~0.14 s with a recursive numeric pose lerp.

techniques.name: Paper finish layer
techniques.how: Low-frequency mottling plus fine noise in overlay blend at ~0.26-0.28 alpha, and a warm radial vignette in multiply, applied over every frame.
techniques.quality_lever: Unifies vector characters and painted sets into one hand-made look.

techniques.name: Restrained additive light
techniques.how: Glow uses 'lighter' blend at alpha ~0.1-0.2 with rays ~0.03; colored light on characters uses 'screen' tints.
techniques.quality_lever: Highlights without washing out or muddying colors.

techniques.name: Cue-driven synthesized score
techniques.how: story.cues() exports event times to JSON; score.mjs places SFX on those times and music on a BPM grid aligned to on-screen beats; two-pass linear loudnorm to -16 LUFS.
techniques.quality_lever: Sound locked to picture with no drift; impacts keep punch; zero licensing risk.

techniques.name: Machine QA gates
techniques.how: Stills at key times, every-Nth-frame samples, FFmpeg contact sheets (dense around fast actions), a frame-to-frame pop detector over STORY.track(t), ffprobe frame-count check, waveform image + EBU R128 for audio.
techniques.quality_lever: Lets the model see and verify its own output; explicit honesty that audio cannot be listened to.

prompting_patterns: Skill frontmatter triggers on animated short / cartoon / mascot animation / storyboard to animate / render to MP4, even without naming the skill.
Sensible defaults instead of interrogation: 1920x1080, 24 fps, 8-20 s, sound on, no captions, one set; user-supplied timings are 'the contract'.
Five beats for 15 s; merge beats rather than rush them; each beat has one readable action.
For existing characters, find an accurate reference first and write proportions as numbers in comments (Clawd decoded from block-character logo in the Claude Code binary).
Progressive disclosure: SKILL.md points to five reference files to read only at the matching step.
Ordered build with stills after each step: beat-table comment -> paint jobs -> static rig -> poseAt(t) -> props/particles/FX.
'Things that bite' list of hard-won pitfalls embedded directly in the skill.
Deliver with an honest summary of what was verified and what could not be (audio not heard).
pipeline: brief (beats, length, sound) -> character reference -> scaffold from template -> story.js (beat table, paint jobs, rig, poseAt, frame) -> stills -> full render + samples + contact sheets + check-motion -> score.mjs on cues -> two-pass loudnorm + mux -> ffprobe verification -> deliver MP4 + runnable project
pitfalls: p5 fails to load without meta charset utf-8.
p5.brush needs p5 2.x and WEBGL; origin is centre.
No real transparency with brush pigment: paper halos around sprites if clip is loose.
Sawtooth bleed on long polygon edges; keep bleed 0.01-0.05 and subdivide.
Repainting brush layers per frame is slow and flickers.
Depth switch while overlapping the occluder cuts the character wrongly.
Raised limbs pivoting inside the body vanish.
Strobing above ~60 px/frame, ~0.7 rad/frame or ~5 Hz cycles.
Glow too strong washes out frame; source-over tints go muddy.
Mirrored sprites read wrong; paint the flipped view.
Missing fonts in headless Chrome; single-pass loudnorm flattens impacts.
Pixabay public API does not serve audio.
evidence: Cloned at commit 653c3ae (2026-09-23); read README, marketplace.json, SKILL.md, all five references, all engine files (core, paint, kit, rig, scene), render.mjs, both tools, new_project.sh, starter story.js, score.mjs, synth.mjs outline, and key sections of the Clawd example story.js; ffprobe'd both demo MP4s and viewed contact sheets of each. No LICENSE file present; GitHub API metadata not accessible from this session.
